 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur
Before

Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari
 On The 2 nd Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 49724 of 2025
 Dr Umesh Setha And Others
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Saurabh Kumar Tiwari - Advocate for the petition
 Shri Somesh Gupta - Panel Lawyer for State.
 Order
With the consent of both the parties, the matter is heard finally.

2. This petition has been preferred by the petitioners under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 challenging the legality, validity, propriety and sustainability of impugned order dated 10.09.2025 passed by Second Additional Sessions Judge, Narmadapuram in Sessions Trial No.66/2023 whereby the petitioners application under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C. has been rejected.
3. Brief facts for adjudication of matter are that the petitioners are the doctors and they are running a hospital in the name of Madan Mohan Memorial Hospital.
The petitioners appointed respondent No.2 as Manager/Accountant for managing the affairs of said hospital as well as their bank affairs.

Thereafter, the respondent No.2 on their behalf was managing NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:65893 2 MCRC-49724-2025 the affairs of said hospital and also maintaining their accounts.
On 11.01.2023, this fact came into the knowledge of the petitioners that respondent No.2-Mohsin Khan

by preparing forged documents like Adhar Card, Pan Card and bank documents obtained near about Rs.2,60,64,344/- business loan from HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance, ICICI Bank,
personal loan from TCFL, CAPRIGHFPL and House Loan from Bandhan Bank as well as he even after receiving the installment and cash money from them not deposited in the bank account and the account of hospital
. The respondent No.2 has also not regularly paid the salary to the employees of staff.
Thus, petitioners made a written complaint with the allegation that the respondent No.2 with the conspiracy of Bank Authorities and Financial Institutions obtained loan in their name.

On said application, the police authority registered a criminal case bearing Crime No.27/2023 at Police Station Kotwali, District Narmadapuram (M.P.) against respondent No.2 under Sections 408, 420,

sentences.text: The police Authority after completing the investigation filed the charge-sheet before the concerning Judicial Magistrate First Class, Narmadapuram on 11.08.2023 and the Judicial Magistrate First Class committed the case vide order dated 11.08.2023 and sent for trial before the Second Additional Sessions Judge, Narmadapuram on 22.06.2023.

5 . The petitioners filed an application under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C. for further investigation on the ground that the respondent No.2 has committed fraud with them and that fraud could not be done with the help and conspiracy of concerned bank, financial institutions and other authorities NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:65893 3 MCRC-49724-2025 and the police authority even after making specific allegation against bank/financial Authorities have not enquired in the matter.
He prays a direction to the police Authorities to investigate the matter further up to the extent of involvement of bank/financial authorities.

6. Learned trial Court vide impugned order dated 10.09.2025 had dismissed the said application only on two grounds first, the petitioners have not moved any application before the concerning Magistrate before whom charge-sheet was filed.
Second, the petitioners have not filed any application after forwarding the matter before the trial Court.
7. Against the said impugned order, the petitioners preferred this petition.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioners advanced the arguments that the order of further investigation may be passed under Section 173 of Cr.P.C.

In the present case, the petitioners have initially alleged that respondent No.2 by conspiring with the bank/financial institutions committed a fraud with them but the police Authority only concluded the investigation against the act of respondent No.2.
The police Authority have never investigated towards the role and conspiracy of bank/financial Authorities.
Mere delay in submitting application for further investigation could not be a ground for dismissal of application.
Under the provisions of Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C. The trial Court have a jurisdiction or authority to pass order of further investigation.
The Sessions Court have exclusive power/authority to trial the case.

It is also submitted that in the case of sessions trial, the power of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:65893 4 MCRC-49724-2025 Magistrate is very limited only up to extent of completion of paper formalities and if such application could not be filed before the Magistrate, the right of the petitioners to submit application before the trial Court could not be forfeited.

In support of that contention, petitioner relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State through Central Bureau of Investigation Vs. Hemendhra Reddy &
Another ETC.

10.

The petitioners in their written complaint specifically alleged that the said forgery and cheating could not be done with the conspiracy of bank/financial authorities and the police authority without conducting any investigation up to that extent filed the charge-sheet.

7. Where the police officer investigating the case finds it convenient so to do, he may furnish to the accused copies of all or any of the documents referred to in Sub-Section (5).

Nothing in this section shall be deemed to preclude further investigation in respect of an offence after a report under Sub-Section (2) has been forwarded to the Magistrate and, where upon such investigation, the officer in charge of the police station obtains further evidence, oral or documentary, he shall forward to the Magistrate a further report or reports regarding, such evidence in the form prescribed; and the provisions of Sub-Sections (2) to (6) shall, as far as may be, apply in relation to such report or reports as they apply in relation to a report forwarded under Sub-Section (2).

sentences.text: Learned trial Court rejected the petitioners' application only on the ground that the petitioners have not filed any application before the Magistrate under Section 173(3) of Cr.P.C. as well as on earlier stage when the case was received for trial after committal.
Under Section 173 of Cr.P.C. there is no limitation for submitting the application for further investigation under the said provision.

Thus, the finding of the Court that the application was not filed at initial stage is not sustainable in the eyes of law and other finding in respect of not submitting any application before Magistrate could not forfeit the right of complainant for submitting application under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C.
before trial Court even after committal.

13. Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the order dated 11.09.2025 passed by learned trial Court rejected the petitioners' application is not justifiable, hence, deserves to be set-aside 14.

The trial Court has yet not dealt with the petitioners application on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:65893 8 MCRC-49724-2025 merit.

Thus it is suitable to remit the case back to the trial Court for a fresh consideration of said I.A.
15.
Considering the same, the impugned order dated 11.09.2025 is set- aside

and the case is remitted back to the trial Court for passing a fresh order on petitioners' application under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C.
16. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
